What I Wanted to Say (WIWS)

Turn what you wanted to say into your own English.

Start with a diary in Japanese, write your own English, then learn from AI corrections, explanations in Japanese, and up to three phrase cards.

Begin with something that happened today. Shape it into what you want to express, then try writing it in English with the words you know. A quiet, paper-inspired journal turns your own experiences into material for learning.

YOUR DAY. YOUR WORDS.

A busy day. A sentence of your own.

Settle in after your day. Write what happened in Japanese, then try it in English with the words you know. Read the corrections and reflect on what you wanted to say. Make room for everyday practice with WIWS.

A few useful answers

When can I download it?+

WIWS is currently under App Store review. A download link will be added after release.

Does AI write the English for me?+

You write your own English first, then review AI corrections. Vocabulary hints are available depending on your device and plan.

Is there a free option?+

The planned trial includes one diary per day for four days from your first entry, with no automatic charge. Pro and Max are paid plans for continued use. Check the app for launch terms.

Does my diary leave my device?+

Diaries are stored locally or in your optional iCloud Drive. AI processing may send diary text or English writing to cloud AI. Some features can use Apple’s on-device AI on supported devices. Availability depends on your device, connection, and plan.

Data & privacy

Diaries are stored on your device, with optional iCloud Drive sync. AI features may send diary text or English writing to cloud AI. The app shows where processing takes place.

This is a pre-release guide. A download link will be added after launch. Check the app for features and plan terms at release.

Your five-step learning loop

Write in Japanese, prepare what you want to express, write your own English, review AI corrections, and revisit today’s phrases. AI feedback may contain errors.

Resume your writing

Save unfinished work and reopen the diary from the home screen. You can also revisit saved diaries and phrase cards.

When AI is unavailable

Check your connection, Apple Intelligence availability, plan, and usage limits. Your existing text is retained when AI is unavailable. Cloud AI requires an internet connection.

Storage and iCloud

Diaries are stored on your device by default. You may enable iCloud Drive storage and sync in settings. Check that important entries are saved before removing the app or changing storage.

Trial and subscriptions

The planned trial provides one diary per day for four days from your first entry, without automatic charging. Pro has monthly and annual subscriptions; Max has a monthly subscription. Use the app’s plan screen to purchase, restore, or manage subscriptions. Saved diaries and phrases remain readable after a trial or subscription ends.

Reminders and app lock

Reminders are optional. Face ID, Touch ID, or passcode locking restricts opening the app; it does not protect diary files stored in iCloud.

Updated October 15, 2026. This page describes data handling for WIWS, currently under App Store review.

Diary storage

Diaries, English drafts, corrections, and phrases are stored on your device by default. If enabled, they are also stored and synced in your own iCloud Drive. iCloud processing follows Apple’s services and your settings.

AI processing

Questions, text preparation, hints, corrections, and phrase extraction may send the necessary diary text, Japanese text, and English writing through a Cloudflare relay to cloud AI from Anthropic or OpenAI. Supported devices can also use Apple’s on-device AI. The app shows processing destinations, which vary by feature, device, and plan.

When on-device AI is available, the raw-diary cloud setting controls questions and text preparation that use the original diary. When on-device AI is unavailable, these AI features use the cloud. Text used for hints and corrections may be sent separately from that setting. If you use your diary unchanged as writing material, it may include the original diary text.

Operational data and feedback

For ordinary AI requests, the developer’s relay does not store or log diary or English text. Operational aggregates include task, model, plan, outcome, processing time, and estimated cost, without text, IP addresses, or device identifiers in those aggregates. External AI providers process requests under their own data terms.

A separate consent-based feedback mechanism may store the selected rating, reasons, optional comment, correction input and output, and model information for quality improvement. Records become eligible for automatic deletion after 90 days without an update. Withdrawing consent allows deletion of the associated feedback data to be requested.

Purchases and abuse prevention

Apple processes purchases. The relay handles purchase verification, installation identifiers, and usage counts to verify subscriptions, manage trials and quotas, and prevent abuse. The developer does not receive credit card details.

Reminders, app lock, and contact

Reminders are scheduled locally. The operating system handles Face ID and Touch ID; the developer does not receive biometric data. App lock does not protect diary files in iCloud. Support email addresses and message content are used to respond and are also processed by the email service.

Manage or delete diaries within the app, and review Apple’s settings for iCloud copies and backups. Contact support@mtk.sh with data questions. This page will be updated when practices change.
